newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cultus looks to boost reserves.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cultus looks to boost reserves.

text.p: Cultus Petroleum NL said on Tuesday it hopes to prove up significant additional gas reserves at Skull Creek in the Otway Basin by March next year.
Managing director Don Beard also said the oil and gas explorer expected profit before abnormals for 1996/97 to range between A$10 million and A$14 million, as in recent years.

"Given the level of activity we have got, we would expect the same sort of number we have seen for the last couple of years," managing director Don Beard told reporters after the annual general meeting. "That's in the 10 to 14 range."

Beard said Cultus saw no impact on its bottom line until it was producing from Skull Creek in the Otway Basin, production increased at the Hutton field in the North Sea, and the Jabiru field off northern Australia was "back to full flight".
Cultus was planning an appraisal well at Skull Creek for March which could add about another 155 billion cubic feet (bcf) of gas reserves to current proven and probable reserves of 292 bcf, he said.
Cultus has proven and probable reserves of 5.5 bcf at Skull Creek, but said in a stock exchange release today it saw potential for another 173.0 bcf.
"We are looking at a significant increase in reserves in the next six months," Beard told reporters.
Cultus recorded a profit before abnormals of A$10.66 million in 1995/96, against A$12.46 million in 1994/95.
An abnormal charge of A$15.30 million, including a A$14.50 million provision for exploration write-offs, led to a 1995/96 net loss of A$4.64 million.
